key_insight: The paper argues that strong math performance in LLMs does not necessarily mean they understand mathematics structurally. It introduces the idea of "mathematical primitives" to diagnose what kinds of underlying math capabilities models actually have and to use that diagnosis to improve post-training.
problem_solved: It tackles the gap between solving math problems correctly and possessing genuine mathematical understanding, aiming to identify which foundational math skills LLMs are missing and how to repair them.
method: Define and use "mathematical primitives" as a probe for structural mathematical understanding.
Systematically diagnose LLM capabilities across different mathematical skills rather than only evaluating final answers.
Leverage the diagnostic findings to guide post-training improvements for better reasoning performance.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this offers a more precise way to evaluate and improve math reasoning beyond benchmark accuracy. It can help build models that are more reliable, interpretable, and robust on complex mathematical tasks.
visual_elements: A pipeline diagram showing diagnosis of mathematical primitives leading to post-training repair
A heatmap of model strengths and weaknesses across different math skills
An infographic comparing "answer correctness" vs. "structural understanding"
Icons for equations, gears, and diagnostic checkmarks to represent probing and repair
paper_title: The Missing Primitive: Diagnosing and Repairing Mathematical Reasoning in Large Language Models
paper_authors: Shuo Xing, Zilin Dai, Chengyuan Qian, Fangzhou Lin, Wenjing Chen
